lint.doctype: <!DOCTYPE html> is missing at the top: without it the browser uses compatibility (quirks) mode and the page may look different.
lint.lang: <html> has no lang attribute (for example lang="en"): screen readers would not know which language to pronounce the text in.
lint.title_missing: <title> is missing from the <head>: it is the name of the tab, of bookmarks and of search results.
lint.charset: <meta charset="utf-8"> is missing: without it, accented letters and other characters may display wrongly.
lint.viewport: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> is missing: on a phone the page would show shrunk, like a desktop version.
lint.duplicate_id: The id “{id}” is already used on another element: an id must be unique (#{id} links, CSS and <label for> only see one).
lint.h1_missing: There is no <h1>: the main heading helps people understand and navigate the page.
lint.h1_multiple: There are {n} <h1> on the page; usually there is just one, with the main topic.
lint.heading_skip: Jumps from <h{prev}> to <h{level}>: do not skip levels, screen readers use headings as an index.
lint.heading_empty: The <h{level}> is empty: a heading without text confuses anyone navigating by headings.
lint.main_missing: There is no <main>: mark the main content so people can jump straight to it.
lint.inline_handler: “{attr}” mixes JavaScript with the HTML; it is cleaner to register the event from a script with addEventListener.
lint.tabindex_positive: tabindex="{value}" alters the natural keyboard order and makes it unpredictable; use 0 or -1.
lint.img_alt: The image has no alt attribute: a screen reader cannot describe it. If it is only decorative use alt="".
lint.img_alt_poor: The alt “{alt}” does not describe the image: say what it shows or what it is for.
lint.img_alt_button: The image button needs an alt attribute saying what it does.
lint.link_name: The link has no text: a screen reader would only say “link”. Add text, or aria-label if it is an icon.
lint.link_vague: The text “{text}” does not say where it leads; out of context (the list of links) it cannot be understood.
lint.target_blank: Links with target="_blank" should carry rel="noopener": without it the opened page can access this one.
lint.link_placeholder: The link points to “#” or is empty: it leads nowhere. Remember to set its destination.
lint.button_name: The button has no text or aria-label: a screen reader would not know what it does.
lint.form_label: The <{tag}> field has no label: add a <label for="id"> (or aria-label). Otherwise nobody knows what to type.
lint.iframe_title: The <iframe> has no title: describe its content for screen reader users.
lint.table_headers: The table has no <th> header cells: without them nobody knows what each column means.
lint.contrast: Low contrast, {ratio}:1 (minimum {min}:1 for {size} text): {fg} on {bg}. Hard to read, especially with poor eyesight or in sunlight.

deprecated_elements.center: use CSS (text-align: center or automatic margins)
deprecated_elements.blink: remove it: blinking is annoying and can harm people with epilepsy
deprecated_elements.frame: use <iframe> or lay out with CSS
deprecated_elements.frameset: use <iframe> or lay out with CSS
